generated_by_note: Single source of truth consumed by generate.py. Edit this file, then re-run `python generate.py` to regenerate every CAD output. Do not hand-edit files under generated/ — they are overwritten on every run.

coordinate_system.origin: Floor level at the illustrative room's left back-wall corner; Station A begins at its configured positive X offset.
coordinate_system.x_axis_mm: +X runs right along the back wall, in the order Station A then Station B (both stations share one wall in the baseline room-plan layout).
coordinate_system.y_axis_mm: +Y runs out from the back wall into the room — the player-standing / depth direction for both stations.
coordinate_system.z_axis_mm: +Z runs up from the finished floor.
coordinate_system.front_view_plane: Front view looks in -Y direction (viewer stands in the room facing the wall) and shows X/Z.
coordinate_system.side_view_plane: Side view looks in -X direction — shows Y (depth) and Z (height).
coordinate_system.top_view_plane: Top view looks in -Z direction (plan view) — shows X (width) and Y (depth).
coordinate_system.note: An L-shaped two-wall layout is a reasonable real-world alternative (keeps the golf sightline out of the shooter's peripheral vision) but is NOT what this generator draws; the single-shared-wall layout here is simpler to keep parametrically correct. Station X-offsets are editable below.

materials.panel_material_assumption: 18mm (nominal 3/4in) cabinet-grade plywood — ASSUMPTION, not a sourced spec. Edit if a different sheet stock is chosen.
materials.sheet_size_note: Standard 8x4ft sheet stock size — common-knowledge stock size, not independently sourced.
materials.sheet_nesting_utilization_note: Deliberately conservative (no true nesting/kerf optimization has been run). Produces a rough, intentionally pessimistic sheet count so the estimate is not falsely optimistic. Replace with a real nesting-software output before ordering material.
materials.kerf_joinery_note: Panel blanks below are nominal outer dimensions only. Saw kerf, rabbet/dado joinery allowances, edge banding, and fastener counterbores are NOT applied — concept stage only, gated to fabrication.
materials.fastener_system_note: Concept assumption: demountable flat-pack hardware (e.g. cam-lock fittings or confirmat-style screws) so each station can be broken down to flat panels for stair transport and reassembled in place. Exact fastener spec/BOM is gated to fabrication.

room_assumptions.note: Room, ceiling and stair/door figures are unmeasured design assumptions. Replace all site dimensions before fabrication. Panel-width checks do not prove clearance around stair turns or for a TV carton.

wall_43.note: Off-the-shelf consumer TV, purchased separately. Active-area width/height below are computed from the diagonal by generate.py (16:9 trigonometry), not a specific model's datasheet — actual bezel/chassis dimensions are unknown until a model is chosen.

wall_55.note: Same caveat as wall_43 — computed active area only, actual chassis TBD.

wall_tv_support.type: Off-the-shelf tilt or full-motion wall-mount arm, purchased separately — explicitly NOT plywood-panel mounting and NOT part of either cabinet.
wall_tv_support.vesa_note: VESA hole pattern is TV-model-specific and unknown until a TV is purchased. No VESA pattern is specified or drilled anywhere in this package.
wall_tv_support.anchorage_note: Stud/structural anchorage into the actual wall is a SCHEMATIC placeholder only (drawn as a generic bracket silhouette). Real fastening must be engineered on site against the actual wall construction (stud layout, masonry, etc.) — GATED, out of scope here.

trackball_pedestal.height_note: 950mm is a provisional standing height to validate with users and a full-size control deck, not an ergonomic guarantee or copied factory dimension.
trackball_pedestal.trackball_diameter_source: 3-inch nominal diameter; actual housing and mounting template must come from the selected part. See parent hardware specification.
trackball_pedestal.control_deck_reserved_zone_note: Outline only — marks where the trackball + buttons will live. NOT a cut hole. Final cutout geometry is gated until the actual trackball/button hardware is selected (no unverified mounting holes belong in a cut file).
trackball_pedestal.strike_clearance_note: Hand-sweep clearance in front of the control deck for a vigorous trackball spin plus adjacent button reach — a design assumption, not a measured ergonomic study.

shooter_console.height_note: 750mm low furniture/holster height is an ergonomic assumption, not a bar-height counter or a commercial gun mounting specification. This console does not support a TV.
shooter_console.holster_spacing_note: 700mm center spacing is a design assumption to validate with actual users and gun/cable envelopes, not a value derived from dividing cabinet width by player count.
shooter_console.gun_reach_envelope_note: Schematic space reservation for gun swing/aim clearance above each holster — NOT a literal gun model.
shooter_console.min_standoff_note: 1700mm from the screen plane is only a starting bench-test distance. Camera/lens/marker geometry and both players' positions determine the real operating zone. Holster position does not establish aiming line of sight.
shooter_console.removable_future_positional_gun_deck_not: Reserved floor footprint for a possible mounted-gun support. The translucent 100mm volume is not a usable gun deck or structural design. No mounting holes, loads, electrical compatibility or approved attachment implied.

games.confidence: Trackball furniture reservation only. Runtime, mounting template and original-I/O compatibility are separate bench gates.
Trackball furniture reservation only; a shared cabinet form does not prove shared runtime or USB I/O compatibility. Preserve the selected donor's complete interfaces.
HD manual documents two guns. Earlier Eagle-era games differ and may use one gun with alternating players; station capability is not game compatibility.

Raw Thrills product service videos and manual confirm two-axis potentiometers, gun vibration hardware, required dongle and I/O. Optical holsters are NOT a faithful 2015 gun assembly; only a future mounting footprint is reserved.

gallery_variants.title: Single universal cabinet
gallery_variants.summary: One display and a movable/swappable control pod; runtime and game-specific I/O remain gated.
gallery_variants.tradeoff: One active game at a time. The trackball pod must clear the gun stance. Geometry is illustrative furniture, not verified play-space.

gallery_variants.title: Two-station modular (BASELINE)
gallery_variants.summary: Trackball furniture plus a shooter console with separate displays; mounted-gun support is an unresolved variant.
gallery_variants.tradeoff: Separates standing trackball and shooter ergonomics without four shells. No claim of common runtime, optical-gun compatibility or exactly half the cost.

gallery_variants.title: Four dedicated cabinets
gallery_variants.summary: One authentic commercial-style cabinet per named game, mirroring a real location-based arcade floor.
gallery_variants.tradeoff: Illustrative allowance for four shells, not a surveyed room fit. Commercial enclosures and player/egress areas may require substantially more space.

gallery_variants.title: Wall rail + mobile controls
gallery_variants.summary: TVs fixed to a wall rail/track; a rolling trackball cart and a rolling gun-holster cart are wheeled into position per game.
gallery_variants.tradeoff: 900mm depth describes stowed furniture only; actual play space must be added. Mobile controls add cable, anchoring and repeatable-calibration work.

gallery_variants.title: Seated deluxe
gallery_variants.summary: Two stations with seated control geometry and stool or bench clearance; the 3D baseline remains standing.
gallery_variants.tradeoff: Reserve more depth for seating. Validate hand height, foot support and mounted-gun reach on a full-size mock-up; do not merely raise the standing deck.
